entities.summary:
Emperor Huai of Jin (司馬熾), personal name Sima Chi (司馬熾), courtesy name Fengdu (豐度), was an emperor of the Jin dynasty.

Born in 280 CE, Emperor Huai ascended to the throne in 290 CE following the death of his father, Emperor Ai of Jin. His reign marked a period of relative stability and prosperity for the Jin dynasty, which had been plagued by internal power struggles and external threats from neighboring states.

One of Emperor Huai's most notable achievements was the implementation of a number of economic reforms, including the standardization of weights and measures, the reorganization of the tax system, and the encouragement of trade and commerce. These reforms helped to stimulate economic growth and improve the overall welfare of his subjects.

Emperor Huai also played a significant role in the development of Confucianism as a state religion, promoting its teachings and establishing new temples dedicated to the veneration of Confucius and other prominent Confucian scholars. This move helped to consolidate power in the hands of the imperial court and legitimize the rule of the Jin dynasty.

Despite his many achievements, Emperor Huai's reign was also marked by a number of challenges, including the threat posed by nomadic tribes from the north and the ongoing instability of the Han state to the west. He died on March 15, 313 CE, succeeded by his son Emperor Hui of Jin.

'When heaven is at peace, one can be at ease.' - Sima Chi (Emperor Huai of Jin)
